stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Ivan Miroshnichenko's agent is working on finding him a trade, noting he has 14 points in 55 career NHL games with the Capitals. He was drafted 20th overall by Washington in 2022.

He has played only three games so far this season, scoring once and averaging 11.05 minutes a night, so the sample is tiny. Still, the details are worth a look. Expected goals, which measure the quality of a player's own chances, put him at 0.43, so his one goal is a bit ahead of what the chances suggested (0.57 above expected). At five-on-five, Washington creates 54% of the expected goals while he is on the ice, and the team does 1.55 percentage points better with him out there than without him. That is a mild positive, not a case that he is being held back.

For Washington, the team sits 8-6-0 and takes 51% of the expected goals overall (53% at five-on-five), so this looks like a depth-chart question more than a team in crisis. For a team looking to add a young winger, the numbers suggest a player who holds his own in limited minutes.

The Athletic reports that Seattle has traded Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and Daily Faceoff describes it as a swap of former first-round picks that gives Wright a change of scenery. Wright went fourth overall in 2022, and Wood went 15th in 2023.

The numbers say this is a swap of two similar, slumping players. So far this season, Wright has 3 goals in 14 games against 3.74 expected goals (the number of goals a player's shot quality would typically produce), a shortfall of 0.74. Wood has 1 goal against 3.12 expected, a gap of 2.12. In that sense Wood has been the unluckier finisher, and his scoring should drift up if his chances keep coming. Both sit below even at five-on-five, with Wright at 47 percent of expected goals and Wood at 47 percent, and both play about 14 minutes a night. Seattle is 8-5-1 despite a 44.9 percent expected goal share, helped by 10.7 more goals than expected. We'd read that as a team outperforming its chances, so the Kraken's record is sturdier than their process. Nashville is 5-4-5 with a 48.9 share, a bit better than its results. Neither player moves the needle much on his own, but Wright gets a new look in Nashville.

Hellebuyck's own start is the soft spot: three games, a .900 save percentage, and goals saved above expected of -0.54, meaning he has let in about half a goal more than an average goalie would have on the same shots. That is a tiny sample, and last season he was 3.43 goals better than expected over 57 games. Winnipeg, at 5-8-3, creates only 45.7 percent of the expected goals and has scored 9.6 fewer goals than its chances suggest. Its goaltending is roughly average (-0.1), so the Jets' problems sit mostly in play and finishing, not in net.

items.desc: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill has managed his team's salary cap situation very well, but Jason Robertson's success could blow up their cap structure. How will the winger's next contract play out?

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Stars GM Jim Nill has handled Dallas's cap well, but that Jason Robertson's production could strain the structure when his next contract comes due. The same day, NHL.com's Tom Gulitti posted that Robertson scored the ninth-fastest hat trick to start a period in NHL history.

Our numbers say the production is real, if a touch hot. Robertson has 8 goals and 18 points in 15 games so far this season, and he's 2.31 goals above what his chances would predict. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and his own sit at 5.7, so some of those 8 goals are finishing luck. The underlying play still holds up: DAL controls 56 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five when he's on the ice, and the team's share of the play is about 7 points better with him than without him. That's the kind of impact a team pays for, which is Nill's problem. Robertson went from 45 goals and 96 points last season, and he was drafted 39th overall in 2017, so the price has climbed steeply. DAL is 9-5-1, but its goals are 2.5 below expected and its goalies are 6.1 saved above expected, so the Stars need Robertson's driving to stay steady.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that fans shouldn't expect Nikita Kucherov to be traded at the deadline unless the Lightning bottom out, noting it has been less than a week since he requested a trade from Tampa Bay.

That condition looks like a long shot on what we've seen so far this season. TBL sit at 9-3-2 for 20 points through 14 games, and they've earned it: the team controls 56% of expected goals (a measure of chance quality, not just shot counts), and 55% at five-on-five. The power play generates 0.76 expected goals per game, while the penalty kill allows just 0.58. That is a team playing well in every phase, so there is no obvious slide to wait for.

The one soft spot is goaltending. TBL's goalies have saved 2.9 goals fewer than expected given the chances they faced, so the record isn't flattered by hot goaltending. If anything, it's the opposite. A team already winning this way, with a goaltending dip, is not one that tends to sell. The sample is small, but it points to a club staying in the race, which keeps Kucherov in Tampa for now.

A goaltending bump (3.6 goals saved above expected) is holding that together, so depth decisions that tilt the underlying play even slightly matter here. Neither player looks like a fantasy factor, and the waiver wire is the likelier destination for both.

Our numbers say one night doesn't change much about Winnipeg. So far this season the Jets have just 44% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and they have scored 9.6 fewer goals than their chances suggest they should have. At 4-8-3, they look more unlucky than doomed, but they are also not winning the chance battle. Montreal, at 9-3-2, sits near even at 50%, with a goalie stopping 5.4 more goals than expected, which flatters the Canadiens.

Samberg is the steady piece. He plays 22.2 minutes a night, and Winnipeg's share of expected goals is nearly 12 points better with him on the ice. He was drafted 43rd overall in 2017, and The Leafs Nation recently pitched him as a Toronto trade target, a sign of how he's valued.

The Hockey News reports that Lightning GM Julien BriseBois is drawing another hard line in contract talks, this time with Nikita Kucherov, after Tampa Bay moved on from Steven Stamkos. As Daily Faceoff's Leafs coverage posted, Elliotte Friedman reports Toronto is among the teams Kucherov would consider being traded to.

On the ice, Kucherov looks every bit the player worth the fight. He has 18 points in 13 games so far this season, and his goals (4) sit almost exactly on his expected goals (4.18), which measures the quality of his chances. So the production is real, not a hot streak. When he plays at 5-on-5, TBL controls about 59% of the expected goals, and the team's share is about six points better with him out there. That matters because TBL's goaltending has been a problem: the team is 4 goals saved above expected in the red. The skaters are carrying it, and Kucherov leads them.

Stamkos is a useful contrast. His 8 goals beat his expected 5.53 by nearly two and a half, and NSH's 5-on-5 share is lower with him on the ice. We'd call his start more fortunate than dominant.
